newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends down as trade, funds sell.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends down as trade, funds sell.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures settled sharply down amid brisk technically-driven selling by the trade and the funds, market sources said.

Prices climbed early, with spot May hitting a fresh contract high of 11.66 cents. But trade selling, particularly by one leading London house, began to pressure the market. Fund buying emerged as sell stops were triggered, pushing most-active July to the day's low of 10.91 cents.
"The trade came in and bought early, the locals went long and suddenly the trade slammed it," Peter Perez, a sugar broker with Merrill Lynch, said.
July closed down 0.17 cent at 11.07 cents per lb, having ranged from 11.28 to 10.91 cents. May ended 0.07 weaker at 11.46, while the back months settled 0.03 higher to 0.02 lower.
Additional selling was expected on Friday, with sell stops cited below 11.00 cents basis July.
Volume was estimated at 41,274 lots compared with Wednesday's official 48,921 lots.
Open interest in May stood at 29,806 lots, down 375 lots as of early Wednesday. July gained 10,470 lots to 87,234 lots.
The last trading day for the May contract is April 30.
Market sources said prices have been supported by dry weather in Europe at the start of the beet growing season, and talk of Russian buying.
The sugar crop in the Brazilian state of Sao Paolo, meanwhile, is forecast at 185.5 million tonnes compared with 170.4 million tonnes last year.
((-- S Rostler, New York Commodities Desk, 212 859 1640))
